strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear motivation for text-driven amodal 3D generation under occlusion
Solid theoretical foundation including spectral analysis, error bounds, and Wasserstein distance guarantees with formal justification for low-pass relaxation
Training-free approach that leverages pre-trained models without requiring fine-tuning, enhancing practical applicability
Comprehensive experimental design with multiple evaluation metrics (CLIP, LPIPS, Point-FID, FID, user studies) and ablation studies demonstrating component contributions
Clever technical contributions including multi-prior consensus mechanism, visibility-aware fusion strategy, and principled dual-branch formulation
Creation of two useful diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D) addressing extreme occlusion and semantic ambiguity
Detailed reproducibility information including implementation details, hyperparameter settings, and dataset curation methodology
weaknesses: Mixed experimental results on ExtremeOcc-3D: CLIP_img metric (0.66) underperforms baseline TRELLIS (0.87); improvements are sometimes modest and inconsistent across metrics
Critical theoretical assumptions (A.2 spectral concentration, A.3 high-frequency mismatch) stated without empirical validation; no verification that these conditions hold in practice

Incremental technical contribution: primarily combines existing techniques (observation-driven generation, semantic priors, flow diffusion) via a relaxation mechanism rather than introducing fundamentally novel ideas

Limited benchmark scale: 264 test cases for ExtremeOcc-3D and 21 curated cases for AmbiSem-3D are relatively small; focus on constrained indoor scenes limits generalization evidence to diverse scenarios
Insufficient failure mode analysis: Section G briefly mentions conflicts between observation and prior but lacks systematic investigation of failure patterns, frequency, and root causes
Reproducibility concerns: no mention of code release, dependence on external pre-trained models (TRELLIS, SAM3D, Z-Image), and apparently arbitrary hyperparameter choices (γ=1.5, ν=1.5, λ=3)
Evaluation metric limitations: CLIP-based metrics may not fully capture semantic alignment; user study with 32 participants is modest; missing quantitative metrics for observation preservation

strengths: Clear problem formulation: Text-driven amodal 3D generation under occlusion is well-motivated with good intuitive explanations (e.g., Figure 1)
Extensive theoretical analysis: Appendix A provides detailed spectral analysis and Wasserstein bounds connecting low-pass relaxation to generation quality
Useful benchmark contributions: ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D provide diagnostic evaluation for occlusion-aware and semantically ambiguous cases, filling a gap in existing evaluation
Consistent empirical improvements: Method shows gains over TRELLIS, SAM3D, and 2D editing baselines on proposed metrics and user preferences
Well-structured presentation: Generally clear writing with informative figures and systematic appendices covering theory, implementation, and evaluation details
weaknesses: Unvalidated theoretical assumptions: Core theoretical contributions depend on Assumptions A.2-A.5 (spectral concentration, band-limited structure) that are never empirically validated. The assumption that semantic intent is low-frequency while errors are high-frequency is oversimplified and questionable
Critical benchmark inadequacy: AmbiSem-3D contains only 21 manually curated cases—far too small for reliable evaluation of semantic ambiguity. This is more toy dataset than rigorous benchmark

Loose theory-practice connection: The spectral analysis in Appendix A justifies low-pass relaxation abstractly, but implementation via attention-logit smoothing (Eq. 8) is straightforward engineering. The gap between what theory proves and what is actually implemented is substantial

Weak evaluation methodology: Heavy reliance on CLIP-based metrics (CLIP_img, CLIP_txt) which have known limitations. User study with only 32 participants and unclear methodology. No evaluation on diverse real-world scenarios beyond synthetic indoor scenes

Incremental technical novelty: Dual-branch generation, low-pass filtering, and multi-prior consensus are established techniques. Main contribution is their combination rather than fundamental innovation

Misleading 'training-free' claim: Method requires pre-trained diffusion models and careful tuning of multiple hyperparameters (visibility mask, σ_d, λ, dilation kernels). Not truly 'training-free' in meaningful sense

Acknowledged but minimized failure modes: Appendix G shows method fails when observation and prior conflict, acting as 'soft concept fusion.' This significant limitation deserves prominence but is buried

Reproducibility concerns: No mention of code/data availability. Custom benchmarks unlikely to be released. Prior construction process complex with apparently ad-hoc hyperparameter choices not well justified
Limited ablation studies: Missing systematic analysis of component contributions (dual-branch necessity, low-pass choice, multi-prior consensus effectiveness)
Evaluation limited to specific domain: Only tested on indoor furniture scenes (3D-FUTURE, 3D-FRONT). Generalization to other 3D domains unclear

strengths: Well-motivated and clearly-articulated problem formulation addressing observation-overfitting in existing 3D generators - a real practical limitation that has been underexplored

Rigorous theoretical analysis: The low-pass relaxation justification via spectral analysis (Section 3.2, Theorem A.4-A.9) is mathematically sound and elegantly connects filtering theory to semantic guidance
Thoughtfully designed dual-branch architecture with principled separation of rigid observation control and relaxed semantic guidance, supported by theoretical guarantees
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple strong baselines, extensive ablations, user study validation (68.52% preference), and multiple evaluation metrics (Point-FID, CLIP, LPIPS)
Novel and valuable benchmark contributions: ExtremeOcc-3D (264 test cases) and AmbiSem-3D (21 curated cases) address gaps in evaluating observation-aware generation and semantic disambiguation
Honest treatment of limitations and failure cases (Section G), acknowledging when observation-prior conflicts lead to 'concept fusion' behavior rather than true amodal completion
Excellent presentation: Clear motivation, well-designed figures (especially Figures 1-3 illustrating the core concept), logical organization, and comprehensive appendices
weaknesses: Limited scale of proposed benchmarks: ExtremeOcc-3D has only 264 test cases and AmbiSem-3D has just 21 manually curated cases, significantly smaller than typical ICML evaluation standards, limiting statistical power and generalization claims

Gap between theoretical assumptions and practice: Assumption A.2 (semantic intent is band-limited) lacks empirical validation and may not universally hold—semantic details are often high-frequency; the visibility mask design involves multiple unjustified hyperparameters (β, γ, λ in Eq. 42)

Modest core technical novelty: The contribution primarily combines established techniques (low-pass filtering, dual-branch architectures, ODE flows) rather than introducing fundamentally new methods; once the problem is motivated, the solution is relatively straightforward

Narrow experimental scope: Evaluation limited to indoor furniture objects from 3D-FUTURE/3D-FRONT; unclear generalization to other object categories, outdoor scenes, or real-world occluded images; all experiments use synthetic data

Incomplete computational efficiency analysis: Only brief mention of 'negligible overhead'; no runtime comparisons against baselines despite dual-branch requiring two evaluations per diffusion step; computational cost for practitioners unclear
Semantic following improvements are modest: While Point-FID improves significantly (e.g., 24.08→27.26 on SAM3D), CLIP score gains are smaller, raising questions about semantic alignment quality

Limited analysis of failure modes and systematic evaluation: 'Concept fusion' behavior acknowledged but not quantified; no breakdown by object category or occlusion pattern; unclear if failures are systematic or edge cases

Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned, hyperparameter selection (e.g., frequency cutoff ρ) not fully characterized, prior image construction process (Appendix C) may be difficult to reproduce exactly

Missing comparisons: No comparison with multi-view conditional generation or recent semantic guidance mechanisms; limited analysis of sensitivity to design choices like the logit smoothing for multi-prior consensus

strengths: Well-motivated dual-objective formulation with rigorous theoretical analysis (Propositions A.4, A.6; Theorems A.8-A.9) connecting low-pass relaxation to semantic guidance stabilization and Wasserstein distance bounds
Addresses an important and underexplored problem—text-driven amodal 3D generation under extreme occlusion—with a training-free approach that leverages existing pretrained models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two complementary benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D for occlusion; AmbiSem-3D for semantic ambiguity) with consistent improvements over multiple baselines (SAM3D, TRELLIS) and metrics
Clear problem illustration and intuitive visualization of core concepts (Figures 1-3); extensive appendices with full proofs, dataset curation details, and metric specifications
Introduces AmbiSem-3D, a valuable new diagnostic benchmark for evaluating semantic branching in 3D generation, valuable for future research
weaknesses: Core theoretical assumptions (A.2: spectral concentration; A.3: high-frequency error) are asserted but not empirically validated on actual semantic velocity fields; Wasserstein bounds depend on unknown constants and don't provide concrete numerical guarantees

Incremental technical novelty—primarily combines established techniques (ODE flows, low-pass filtering, multi-prior consensus, visibility masking) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts; low-pass filtering for noise suppression is well-known in signal processing

Limited evaluation scope: benchmarks are small-scale (264 ExtremeOcc-3D test cases, 21 core AmbiSem-3D cases); only two 3D generation backbones tested (SAM3D, TRELLIS); no user studies despite claiming perceptual improvements; min-LPIPS metric biases toward diverse predictions over single best completions

Prior image construction is somewhat artificial (sampling 'different object of same category' for ExtremeOcc-3D) and introduces external dependencies (Z-Image generation for AmbiSem-3D); no systematic robustness analysis for poor-quality priors

Visibility mask computation (Appendix F) appears ad-hoc with dataset-specific parameters (β=1.5, γ=1.5, λ=3.0); limited ablation studies (Figures 5-6); design choices (Gaussian blur, logit smoothing, linear cutoff schedule) lack principled justification; shallow failure mode analysis in Section H

No code release promised; method depends on specific versions of external models (SAM3D, TRELLIS, CLIP, Point-E); stochastic elements (prior sampling, random object selection) underspecified; dataset licensing may restrict reproducibility; results lack error bars or confidence intervals
